Learn how to configure feature flags and customize the theme of the Vonage Video iOS App.

Welcome! In this tutorial you will configure the **Vonage Video iOS App** (`vonage-video-ios-app`), a Swift application built with [Tuist](https://tuist.io). Building it natively requires **Xcode 26+** and **SwiftLint**, but you won't need either of those for this tutorial — everything you'll do here happens through JSON configuration files and Python/shell generator scripts run from a terminal.

Unlike the sibling React app tutorials, which split feature-flag configuration and theme customization into two separate tutorials, this tutorial covers **both** in a single walkthrough, since the iOS app manages both concerns through similar generator scripts.

## In this tutorial you will

- Set up the shared backend server and generate the app's environment constants
- Explore how feature flags are structured in `VERA/Config/app-config.json`
- Edit feature flags and regenerate the corresponding Swift configuration
- Explore how color, border radius, and typography tokens are structured in `VERA/Theme/semantics.json`
- Edit theme tokens and regenerate the corresponding color assets
- Confirm your changes by inspecting generator output and generated files

{% aside type="caution" %}
This Codespace does not include Xcode or macOS, so you cannot build, run, or preview the iOS app here. Verification in this tutorial is limited to confirming that generator scripts complete successfully and that the expected values show up in the generated Swift and asset catalog files — never a simulator, a device build, or a browser preview.
{% /aside %}

Let's start by setting up the backend server and generating the app's environment constants.

The iOS app doesn't have a backend of its own. It talks to the same Node.js server the Vonage Video React App uses, running on port **3345**. Before you can generate environment constants for the iOS app, you need that backend running and reachable from this Codespace.

## Start and Expose the Backend

{% steps %}

1. Start (or confirm) the backend server is running on port **3345**.

2. Click the **Ports** tab at the bottom of the Codespace, then right-click on port **3345** → **Port Visibility → Public**.

{% /steps %}

{% aside type="caution" %}
The port must be public for the iOS app's generated environment constants to reach the backend. If it's still private, requests from the app will fail.
{% /aside %}

## Export the Backend URL

Copy the forwarded address for port 3345 from the **Ports** tab, then export it as `BASE_API_URL`:

```sh
export BASE_API_URL=https://<codespace-subdomain>-3345.app.github.dev
```

Only the `<codespace-subdomain>` portion differs between Codespaces — the rest of the URL stays the same.

## Generate the Environment Constants

With `BASE_API_URL` exported, run the environment generator script from the `VERA/` directory:

```sh
./Scripts/generateEnvironmentConstants.sh
```

## How It's Structured

`app-config.json` is organized into four top-level sections, one per area of the app:

```json
{
  "videoSettings": {
    "allowBackgroundEffects": true,
    "allowCameraControl": true,
    "allowVideoOnJoin": true,
    "defaultResolution": "640x480"
  },
  "audioSettings": {
    "allowAdvancedNoiseSuppression": true,
    "allowAudioOnJoin": true,
    "allowMicrophoneControl": true,
    "allowAudioDiagnostics": true
  },
  "waitingRoomSettings": {
    "allowDeviceSelection": true,
    "allowSettings": true
  },
  "meetingRoomSettings": {
    "allowArchiving": true,
    "allowCaptions": true,
    "allowChat": true,
    "allowDeviceSelection": true,
    "allowEmojis": true,
    "allowFeedback": true,
    "allowPictureInPicture": true,
    "allowScreenShare": true,
    "allowSettings": true,
    "defaultLayoutMode": "activespeaker",
    "showParticipantList": true
  }
}
```

- **`videoSettings`** — controls camera behavior and video quality before and during a call.
- **`audioSettings`** — controls microphone behavior and audio diagnostics.
- **`waitingRoomSettings`** — controls what participants can do while waiting to be admitted.
- **`meetingRoomSettings`** — controls in-call features once a participant has joined the meeting room.

## Representative Flags

Here's a closer look at some of the most commonly changed flags:

| Flag | Section | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allowChat` | `meetingRoomSettings` | boolean | `true` | Shows or hides the in-call chat panel |
| `allowArchiving` | `meetingRoomSettings` | boolean | `true` | Enables or disables session recording (archiving) controls |
| `allowCaptions` | `meetingRoomSettings` | boolean | `true` | Enables or disables live captions during a call |
| `allowEmojis` | `meetingRoomSettings` | boolean | `true` | Enables or disables the emoji reaction picker |
| `allowScreenShare` | `meetingRoomSettings` | boolean | `true` | Enables or disables the screen-share button |
| `allowBackgroundEffects` | `videoSettings` | boolean | `true` | Enables or disables virtual background/blur effects |
| `defaultResolution` | `videoSettings` | string | `"640x480"` | Sets the default camera capture resolution used when a call starts |
| `defaultLayoutMode` | `meetingRoomSettings` | string | `"activespeaker"` | Sets the default video layout (e.g. active speaker vs. grid) when a meeting room loads |

## How It's Structured

`semantics.json` nests every token under `themes.vonage`, split into three groups: `colors`, `borderRadius`, and `typography`:

```json
{
  "themes": {
    "vonage": {
      "colors": {
        "light": { "primary": "#9941FF", "background": "#F5F0FD", "...": "..." },
        "dark":  { "primary": "#B27BF2", "background": "#26044D", "...": "..." }
      },
      "borderRadius": {
        "none": 0, "extra-small": 2, "small": 4, "medium": 8, "large": 12, "extra-large": 24
      },
      "typography": {
        "font-family": "Inter",
        "desktop": { "headline": { "font-size": "66px", "line-height": "88px", "font-weight": 500 }, "...": "..." },
        "mobile":  { "headline": { "font-size": "32px", "line-height": "40px", "font-weight": 500 }, "...": "..." }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`colors.light` / `colors.dark`** — Separate color palettes for each mode. Both modes use the same set of semantic token keys.
- **`borderRadius`** — Six named tokens controlling the corner rounding of buttons, cards, and dialogs.
- **`typography`** — A shared `font-family`, plus separate `desktop` and `mobile` type scales. Both scales use the same named tokens, just with different point sizes.
